Solana 上的 Hook 叙事，不是 Uniswap v4 那套池子回调，而是把规则写进代币转账本身。主线是 Token-2022 的 transfer hook，再叠一层发射台，让 meme 发射时自带防狙击、销毁、持币分红，而不是毕业后靠网站或机器人继续执行。

和以太坊 Hook 的差别
以太坊 v4 的 hook 挂在池子上。创建时写进 PoolKey，在 swap、加减流动性前后插入逻辑，可以改费率甚至改定价。Solana 原生对应物是 Token-2022 transfer hook：mint 指定一个程序，每一笔转账（买入、卖出、钱包互转）都会调用它。转账违反规则就直接失败。规则在链上，不依赖发射台网站一直在线。

这带来一个硬限制。标准 transfer hook 基本只能说 yes 或 no，不能从这笔交易里切一块出来销毁或打给持币人。钱包互转和池子交易在转账层看起来一样，所以「只对买卖收费、互转不收费」做不干净。Solana 上现在的叙事，就是在补这个缺口。

现在实际在讲的三层
1. 协议层：Token-2022 transfer hook

这是底料，不是新发明。Hooked 的文档写得很直白：发射时选定规则，例如单钱包持仓不超过 1%、或只允许钱包互转；Solana 在转账内部执行；发射方和平台事后都不能关掉。毕业（graduation）才是少数能拿掉 hook 的路径，而且只对会毕业的曲线生效。少数类型标明可改：创建者可编辑、持币人 DAO 投票、或交给 AI agent。

2. 发射层：把 hook 产品化

这是 2026 年 9 月底到 10 月才热起来的交易叙事，项目都还很小。

Hooked（@Hoookedpad，https://t.co/UcUdZ4VN0O）在 Meteora bonding curve 上发币。预设包括持仓上限、水下回血（每 5 分钟把手续费锅按浮亏比例打给还没回本的持币人）。10 月 8 日他们又推了「Hooked standard」：自建 token program、DEX 和发射台，声称 hook 不再只返回 yes/no，而是返回金额，从而在每笔交易上给持币人打 SOL、销毁一部分、或付给创建者，并且毕业后规则仍在。同时上了 AI 写 hook，编译器检查后再发射。平台币 HOOKED 的 Meteora 池大约只有数万美元流动性，属于早期盘，不是基础设施龙头。
Hooker（@hookerdotfun）走另一条分发：在 https://t.co/ZJG4fAamwc 和 Pons 上给发射加规则，并做 Meteora 到 https://t.co/ZJG4fAamwc 的毕业上限自定义，也可以选择一直留在 Meteora、hook 不摘。关注度更低。
周边还有 Ember 这类前端在喊「先上 Meteora，下一步上 hooks」，本质仍是发射分发，不是新 AMM。
3. 流动性层：Meteora，不是 hook 本身

Solana 发射的钱大多流过 Meteora 的 DBC（动态 bonding curve）、DLMM 和 DAMM v2。10 月 6 日 Meteora 发布 DLMM Pro：费率随市场成熟递减、LP 仓位 NFT 化、发射参数可配，目前还在 waitlist。这是「可定制 AMM」，和 transfer hook 相邻，但不是同一个机制。Meteora 才是这条链上有真实费用的资产；hook 发射台还在抢叙事。

作为对照，DexPaprika 10 月 9 日口径下 Meteora 三套程序 24 小时成交约 6.9 亿美元，其中 DAMM v2 约 4.67 亿美元。Hooked 自己的池子是万美元级。

叙事在卖什么
卖点就一句：https://t.co/qTudXY3cf9 式发射规则太单一，毕业后税率、销毁、持仓上限全靠项目方自觉；hook 让规则在转账时强制执行，毕业后仍在。玩法模板已经在抄以太坊那套：防狙击费、持有越久卖出税越低、越跌销毁越多、单日卖出上限、持币人 SOL 分红、水下补贴。

和 v4 的关键差异是价值捕获位置。以太坊 hook 吃的是池子手续费和自定义曲线；Solana 这波吃的是发射注意力和代币自带的转账税。平台币能不能分到这些税，要逐个合约看，不能默认「有 hook 就有平台税」。10 月 1 日还有一份针对 Hooked 的指控复核：约 2080 SOL 来自 HOOKED 自己曲线和毕业后流动性仓位的创建者手续费，不是从发射台 flywheel 里转走的。说明这个赛道已经开始打费用归属战。

怎么看
Solana 的 Hook 是 meme 发射规则层，不是 Uniswap v4 的池子可编程层。能对标的是「Token-2022 + 发射台」，不是「自定义 AMM」。Meteora 是流动性底座，Hooked / Hooker 是在上面贴规则的前端和代币标准实验。

跟踪时只看三件事：规则是不是毕业后仍由 token program 执行，而不是网站开关；hook 能不能改金额，还是只能拒绝转账；手续费进的是平台金库、创建者钱包，还是持币人。AI 写 hook 会把恶意或写错的规则规模化，以太坊上 hook 合约大量不安全的问题，在这里会换成「转账直接失败或税被抽走」。

tweets.text:
$hooked Vs $BORDR 

Maybe just bet on the house $MET lolz

It's a Solana launchpad copycat fight from the last two days. Hooked and Bordrless (often written Borderless) are both selling the same idea: memecoins whose rules live inside the token, not in a bot or a website the team can turn off.

**What each one actually is**

Hooked (`@Hoookedpad`, token `HOOKED`) showed up in late September as a Meteora launchpad. Creators pick rules (max wallet, sell caps, anti-dump, market hours) and Solana's Token-2022 transfer hook rejects any transfer that breaks them. A transfer hook can only say yes or no. It runs after balances change and cannot rewrite the amount.

Bordrless (`https://t.co/K2w1VKt8WT`, `@bordrlessdex`, token `BORDR`, `6Mix12…bordr`) shipped a different stack on October 7: its own token program, DEX, launchpad, and bridge, open-sourced under Apache-2.0. Their pitch is that a Token-2022 hook is too weak, so they built Uniswap-v4-style hooks that run before and after a trade and can change the amount — pay holders in SOL, burn a cut, pay the creator, age-based exit fees. Rules are fixed at launch. The programs still have an upgrade authority until an audit.

**The drama**

On October 8, about a day after Bordrless deployed, Hooked announced "the Hooked standard": its own token program, DEX, and launchpad, where a hook answers with amounts. Same feature list: pay holders in SOL, burn part of the trade, pay the creator, plus a bridge.

Bordrless holders immediately called it a paste. Replies on the announcement said Hooked copied the open GitHub and swapped the name. One post put it as "they literally stole his code and put HOOKED instead of BORDERLESS." The Hooked side says Bordrless was the vamp — a new pad built to ride Hooked's September attention — and that shipping the same capability back in hours is fair game. A reply in that thread notes the repo is Apache-2.0, so forking is the point, and calling it theft only when the bigger name does it is picking a side.

Apache-2.0 does allow reuse and modification. It also requires keeping copyright notices and stating what you changed. Nobody has posted a verified diff showing whether attribution was stripped, so the "stolen code" claim is an allegation, not a proven license breach.

Underneath the bag war, the product fight is real: Token-2022 hooks can only veto a transfer. A custom program can tax, burn, and redirect on the trade itself. Bordrless published that design first. Hooked had the audience and the earlier pad, then shipped the same class of system the next day. Both are days old, upgradeable, and thinly liquid.

I've written two research posts on solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE before, and after continuing to follow what the team has been building, I think there's still quite a lot worth digging into here

What keeps me interested in solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE isn't simply the chart or the number of tokens burned. It's how the team is trying to build a differentiated launchpad on Solana

There is no shortage of launchpads in this market. Creating a token has become easier than ever, but building an ecosystem with real users, sustainable volume, and recurring revenue is a completely different challenge

Let's break it down

1. What makes Hooked different?

Hooked's original differentiation comes from Token-2022 Transfer Hooks, which allow creators to enforce trading rules directly on-chain, including anti-bundle, anti-dump, max wallet limits, holder vesting, and market hours

Instead of relying entirely on frontends or external bots, these rules can be checked during the token transfer process itself

But there's an important distinction

With a Graduating Curve, certain hooks can be removed after graduation. With a Permanent Curve, they remain active

The hook program can also be upgraded through the deploy authority, meaning trust in the team hasn't completely disappeared

Another limitation is compatibility. Some wallets or applications may fail to process transfers if they don't provide the additional accounts required by a particular hook

So while Transfer Hooks offer interesting functionality, they aren't an exclusive moat. Other Solana launchpads can build similar features

The real question is whether Hooked can turn that technical differentiation into a product people consistently want to use

2. Hooked is building more than a traditional launchpad

What interests me is how the team is expanding beyond basic token launches into a platform where creators can design more complex tokenomics

Hooked Standard is one of the more important developments

Instead of simply allowing or rejecting transfers, rules can distribute rewards to holders, burn tokens, or redirect fees based on specific conditions

According to the team's design, Hooked Standard also introduces its own token program and DEX, allowing certain rules to remain active after graduation

Paired Launches take another approach

Tokens no longer have to be paired exclusively with SOL. They can be paired with supported assets such as xStocks, gold, silver, or other tokens, while holders can receive rewards in the paired asset itself

The team states that paired launches carry a 3% fee, with Hooked's portion following the same flywheel mechanism as standard launches

Beyond that, the team has introduced several other mechanisms

Underwater Hook uses a SOL pot to distribute payments approximately every five minutes to holders sitting at a loss, with payouts based on the size of their losses until the pot is exhausted

The Grudge introduces rules around selling and buying back tokens, potentially applying taxes or restrictions to returning buyers, with the tax directed toward solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE buybacks and burns

Loans allow holders to use tokens as collateral to borrow SOL under the proposed mechanism, while Lock & Earn, Social Trading Wars, and AI-assisted Hook Creation expand the platform's functionality further

I like the direction here

Hooked is trying to give creators more control over how tokens behave, how value is distributed, and how holders interact with the ecosystem

But shipping features and proving adoption are two different things

We still need to see how many users actually interact with these mechanisms, whether they generate meaningful trading volume, and whether that activity continues after the initial incentives disappear

3. The flywheel remains the most important part of the thesis

According to the published mechanism, every trade on a standard bonding curve generates a 1% protocol fee

85% goes toward market buying and burning solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE, while the remaining 15% is allocated to development

This creates a direct relationship between platform activity and demand for the native token

In my first research post, the dashboard showed approximately 25.7M solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE burned and 865 SOL used for buybacks

By my second post, those figures had increased to 38.07M burned and 1,882 SOL in buybacks

The official October 8 snapshot showed approximately 61.49M solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE burned, representing 6.15% of the total supply, with around 3,693 SOL used for buybacks

That's meaningful progress, especially considering the flywheel continued operating while the chart experienced a significant correction

However, there's something I think people should pay more attention to

The total amount burned matters less than whether the burn rate can be sustained

61.49M tokens burned is a cumulative figure

It proves the mechanism is functioning, but it doesn't prove revenue will continue growing once attention fades

What matters more is how much SOL the platform can consistently generate for buybacks each day

If trading volume remains healthy after the initial hype, the thesis becomes considerably stronger

But if most revenue comes from short-lived launch activity, the buyback rate could slow down significantly

And that would change how the market values the flywheel

4. Nearly 1,000 launches, but where is the real runner?

This remains my biggest question about Hooked

The number of tokens launched has grown from nearly 500 to around 994 in the snapshot I reviewed

But the leading tokens on the platform still haven't demonstrated the kind of sustained success I'm looking for

$HAMSTER was sitting around $1.5–1.6M market cap, $FOMO around $840K, and solana:3ykvcjrzbb5nyJRnzHVEA12sQsZfnTijwxUusN4f8R3R near $142K

Most of the remaining tokens were trading at considerably lower valuations

Interestingly, both $HAMSTER and $FOMO were trading at higher market caps when I wrote my previous research

That doesn't automatically make them failures

But it does show that Hooked hasn't yet produced a convincing runner capable of maintaining strong liquidity, holder retention, and trading activity after the initial hype

A launchpad can create thousands of tokens, but if most of them generate volume for only a few hours before fading away, the ecosystem remains dependent on fresh speculative capital

What I want to see is a token that graduates, retains liquidity and holders, and continues generating meaningful volume over time

Because tokens launched on Hooked don't need to hold solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE to support the flywheel

They need to generate trading activity that produces protocol fees

A single token maintaining consistent volume over several days could create more value than hundreds of launches that disappear almost immediately

And so far, I still haven't seen a runner convincing enough to validate that part of the thesis

5. Could solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE follow the path of $STONK or $PONS?

I've noticed some researchers and traders comparing Hooked with StonkFun and PONS because their models connect platform activity with native token buybacks and burns

From a narrative perspective, I understand the comparison

StonkFun is also building a launchpad supporting different asset types, while PONS previously attracted significant attention through its flywheel mechanism

But having a similar fee structure doesn't automatically mean Hooked deserves a similar valuation

Market cap isn't determined solely by the percentage of fees allocated to buybacks

It also depends on users, liquidity, launch quality, competitive positioning, and the ability to generate recurring revenue

Transfer Hooks provide technical differentiation, but the underlying technology isn't exclusive to Hooked

Other launchpads can develop similar functionality

Hooked's real moat needs to come from users, trading volume, and its ability to retain successful projects

If Hooked can demonstrate that, comparisons with larger launchpads will become much more meaningful

Until then, I see those comparisons as a narrative that can attract attention, not proof of long-term value

6. The creator wallet remains an unanswered question

solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE: A Solana Launchpad With a Different Idea

solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE - @Hoookedpad

I bought solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE on the first dip after launch.

I'm obviously biased because I hold it, but after digging properly into what Hooked has actually built, I think there's a much stronger thesis here than simply betting on another Solana launchpad.

The basic idea is simple:

Hooked lets people launch tokens with rules built directly into the token itself.

That sounds like a small difference.

It isn't.

A thread:

WHAT HOOKED ACTUALLY DOES

Most token launchpads give you a token, a liquidity pool and a bonding curve.

Hooked adds programmable rules.

For example, a creator can launch a token where:

Wallets can't hold more than a certain percentage

Early buyers have vesting restrictions
Selling is capped
Trading is only allowed during certain hours
Particular wallets are allowed to interact with the token
The important part is that these rules aren't enforced by a bot or by Hooked's website.

They're built into the token using Solana's Token-2022 Transfer Hook technology.

Every time the token moves, Solana calls the hook program.

The program can read the transfer and refuse it.

If it refuses, the transaction fails.

Think of it like putting the security guard inside the door rather than hiring someone to stand outside it.

The guard can stop the transfer.

It cannot rewrite the economics of it.

WHY THIS MATTERS

Crypto launches have a long-standing problem with bots, snipers, bundled wallets and early holders dumping on everyone else.

Hooked is trying to make some of those problems part of the token's actual design.

The platform currently offers dozens of rules across dozens of hook programs on Solana mainnet.

Hooked says 17 rules have been proven enforcing inside live Meteora swaps, while others were tested on devnet before going live.

And this isn't just sitting on a roadmap.

The platform currently shows roughly 950 token launches.

That's obviously not the same thing as having 950 successful projects.

Most won't be.

But it does prove people are actually using the product.

THERE ARE SOME IMPORTANT LIMITS

On the default graduating curve, Meteora removes the hook in the buy that fills the curve.

That means the rule stops after graduation.

Permanent curves keep the rule for the life of the token.

Some token types can also have their rules replaced later.

That's important because the idea of "rules enforced on-chain" isn't quite as absolute as it first sounds.

The underlying enforcement programs are also currently upgradeable by Hooked.

That's something I'm watching closely.

THE PART I CARE ABOUT MOST: solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE CAPTURES PLATFORM ACTIVITY

This is where the investment thesis gets more interesting.

Hooked has a fee mechanism connected to activity on the platform.

Every trade on a Hooked curve pays a 1% fee.

According to the docs, 85% of Hooked's share is used to buy and burn solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE, with 15% going to development.

That creates a potential link between:

More launches

More trading

More fees

More solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE bought and burned

That's the flywheel I'm actually investing in.

Not the word "AI".

Not a fancy roadmap.

Not a promise that the token will go up.

The question is whether Hooked can become a platform people genuinely want to use.

If it does, solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE has a mechanism for capturing some of that activity.

THE TECHNOLOGY IS MORE AMBITIOUS THAN A LAUNCHPAD

Hooked also has what it calls the Hooked standard.
This goes beyond simply allowing or rejecting a transfer.

Its own token program and DEX are designed so that hooks can control things like:

Fees

Burns

Holder rewards

Lock & Earn

Loans

Buyer rewards

Social trading

Paired tokens

These standard programs are upgradeable by Hooked.

That's a different trust model from a fixed Token-2022 hook configuration.

And this is where I think the longer-term opportunity sits.

If programmable tokens become more common, Hooked isn't just a place to launch them.

It could become part of the infrastructure used to build them.

That's a much bigger market.

It's also the part that still has to be earned.

THE TOKEN

Hooked tokens generally start with a supply of 1 billion.

On the Hooked standard, roughly 75% of supply is sold through the curve, with the remaining 25% reserved for liquidity at graduation.

There's also an important positive here for me:

There isn't an obvious giant VC unlock schedule hanging over solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE.

That doesn't eliminate selling pressure.

Early holders can still sell.

Recent screens have put the top 10 wallets around 21–25% of supply, so wallet distribution still needs watching.

At the time of writing, solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE is sitting around a $7M market cap.

Those numbers move quickly, so I'd treat them as a snapshot rather than gospel.

WHAT I LIKE

The biggest positive is that the product is already live.

Hooked isn't telling us what it plans to build.

There are already hundreds of launches, dozens of rules and multiple pieces of infrastructure operating on Solana mainnet.

The buyback is also showing executed burns rather than only being a promise.

I also like that the core concept uses existing Solana functionality rather than requiring an entirely new blockchain.

And the token has a clearer connection to platform usage than most small-cap launches.

If the platform generates meaningful volume, the buyback mechanism has something to work with.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE

The biggest issue is adoption.

Transfer Hooks are a Solana feature.

Hooked doesn't own the underlying technology, which means another team can build something similar.

So the moat can't simply be:

"We invented programmable tokens."

They didn't.

The moat has to become the product, rule library, liquidity, creators and users.

There's also a genuine UX problem.

Some Hooked tokens require wallets and applications that understand Token-2022 transfer hooks.

Hooked itself says a standard wallet Send button can fail for hooked tokens because the extra accounts required by the hook aren't included.

That's something I'd want to see improve.

THE BEAR CASE

The biggest risk is that Hooked builds clever infrastructure for a market that doesn't care.

Maybe most token creators don't want programmable rules.

Maybe they just want the easiest possible launch.

Maybe Pump-style platforms continue to dominate because simplicity wins.

And even if Hooked gets hundreds or thousands of launches, that doesn't mean those launches generate meaningful economic activity.

That's what I'd watch.

Not the number of tokens launched.

I'd rather see 50 genuinely active launches generating serious volume than 5,000 dead tokens.

The other risk is competition.

If a larger launchpad copies Hooked's best features and has a much bigger user base, Hooked needs to give creators a reason to stay.

That's the real test.

MY VERDICT

I think solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE is one of the more interesting small cap infrastructure bets I've come across recently.

The reason isn't that I think every token launched on Hooked will succeed.

Most won't.

It's that the team is building around a genuinely useful idea:

Tokens that can have their own rules enforced at the protocol level.

The platform is already live.

The rule system is expanding.

People are using it.

And solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE has a documented mechanism that can connect curve fees back to the token through buybacks and burns.

At roughly a $8M market cap, I think the market is still treating this primarily as another tiny Solana launchpad.

I'm buying the possibility that it becomes something more than that.

What would change my mind?

If launch activity stops growing, trading volume disappears, creators move elsewhere, the buyback stops matching the fee docs, or the programmable-token idea proves to be something nobody actually needs, I'd reassess quickly.

For now, I'm happy holding my solana:C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE position and watching whether the product turns early traction into a real ecosystem.

This is my research and opinion, not financial advice.
